review.tagline: MCP server that keeps raw tool output out of the context window
review.summary: Context Mode is an MCP server that runs analysis in a sandbox so raw tool output stays out of the agent's context. It logs edits, git operations and tasks in SQLite, indexes them with FTS5, and retrieves relevant events via BM25 after compaction. It ships hooks and routing for Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Copilot, Cursor and others.
review.audience: Developers running coding agents who hit context limits and compaction loss
strengths: Sandbox tools cut raw output; README cites 315 KB reduced to 5.4 KB
Session events stored in SQLite with FTS5/BM25 retrieval after compaction
Hooks for Claude Code, Gemini CLI, VS Code and JetBrains Copilot, Copilot CLI, Cursor
Claude Code plugin install, plus MCP-only option via npx
weaknesses: Elastic License 2.0, not an OSI open-source license
Non-hook platforms need a manual routing file copy
Most platforms require Node.js >= 22.5 or Bun
Savings figures are README examples, not independent benchmarks
needs: Models: Claude Code, Gemini CLI, VS Code Copilot, JetBrains Copilot, GitHub Copilot CLI
